chunks: Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (عليه السلام), ‘May I be sacrificed for you, by what is the Imam recognized?’ He said: ‘By qualities. As for the first of them, it is that there has preceded from his father concerning him an indication toward him, so that it may be a proof against them. He is asked and he answers; and if one remains silent from asking him, he initiates; and he informs of what will be tomorrow; and he speaks to the people in every tongue.’

Then he said to me, ‘O Abu Muhammad, I shall give you a sign before you rise.’ It was not long before a man from the people of Khurasan entered upon us. The Khurasani spoke to him in Arabic, and Abu al-Hasan (عليه السلام) answered him in Persian. So the Khurasani said to him, ‘By Allah, may I be sacrificed for you, nothing prevented me from speaking to you in Khurasani except that I thought you did not know it well.’ He said, ‘Glory be to Allah! If I were not able to answer you, then what excellence would I have over you?’

Then he said to me, ‘O Abu Muhammad, the Imam is not unaware of the speech of any among the people, nor of a bird, nor of a beast, nor of anything in which there is a spirit. So whoever does not possess these qualities is not an Imam.’

key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: The divinely appointed Imam, recognized through specific signs and qualities.
key_terms.بِإِشَارَةٍ: By explicit indication from the previous Imam toward his successor.
key_terms.بِخِصَالٍ: By distinct characteristics or qualities that identify the true Imam.
key_terms.بِكُلِّ لِسَانٍ: In every language, indicating universal communicative knowledge.
key_terms.حُجَّةً: A binding proof against the people, leaving no excuse after clarification.
key_terms.عَلَامَةً: A sign given as demonstrative evidence of the Imam’s status.
key_terms.فَضْلِي: My excellence or merit, referring to the distinguishing superiority of the Imam.
key_terms.لَا يَخْفَى عَلَيْهِ: Nothing is hidden from him, referring here to speech and communication.

ai.seo_question: How is the Imam recognized according to this hadith from al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the Imam is recognized through divinely granted signs, including explicit designation by the preceding Imam, immediate and authoritative knowledge, foreknowledge by Allah’s permission, and the ability to speak with people in every language. It presents these qualities as proofs of the Imam’s divine authority and as distinguishing marks that set the true Imam apart from others.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Mihran, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! By what is the Imam<sup>asws</sup> recognised?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By certain characteristics. As for its first, so he<sup>asws</sup> would be with something which would have preceded from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> by indicating to him<sup>asws</sup> in order for it to be a proof upon them (people); and he<sup>asws</sup> would be asked, so he<sup>asws</sup> would answer, and if they (people) are silent from him<sup>asws</sup>, he<sup>asws</sup> would initiate and inform with whatever regarding the next day; and he<sup>asws</sup> would speak to the people in every language.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Abu Muhammad! I<sup>asws</sup> shall give you a sign before you would be arising’. So it was not long before a man from the people of Khurasan came over to us. So the Khurasani spoke in Arabic and Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> answered him in Persian. So the Khurasani said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Nothing prevented me from speaking to you<sup>asws</sup> in Khurasani language (Persian) apart from that I thought that you<sup>asws</sup> might not be good at it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! When I<sup>asws</sup> am not good in answering you, so what would be my<sup>asws</sup> merit over you?’

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Abu Muhammad! The Imam<sup>asws</sup> is such that no one’s speech is concealed upon him, neither from the people, nor a bird, nor an animal, nor anything in which is a soul. So the one who does not have this characteristic in him, so he isn’t an Imam<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ahmad ibn Mihran has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali from abu Basir who has said that he asked the following from abu al-Hassan (a.s.) , “May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, what is the proof to know the Imam (a.s.) ?”

He said, “Through several qualities. The first thing is that his father must have said to this effect about him so that it could be considered a proof up on him. And that when asked he would answer and if one remain silent he would begin to speak on the issue and inform of the things that would happen the next day that can speak to people in everyone’s own language.”

Then he said to me, “O abu Muhammad, allow me to give you a sign before you stand up to go. Not very long after this a man from Khurasan came in. The man from Khurasan spoke to the Imam in Arabic but abu al-Hassan (a.s.) answered him in Persian. The man from Khurasan said, “I swear by Allah, “May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, the only thing that stopped from speaking to you in Persian was I thought you might not know Persian.” He then said, “Glory belongs to Allah, If would not b e able to answer you (in Persian) than how would have any excellence over you?”

He said to me, “O abu Muhammad, “No one’s language is unknown to the Imam (a.s.) nor the language of birds, animals and any living things. Whoever would not have these qualities he is not A number of our people has narrated from Imam.”
